questions.gloss: How does AIOS know what it is?

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know its current architecture?
questions.note: boundary count, import graph, relationship map

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know which capabilities exist and which do not?
questions.note: declared capabilities only; INFERRED — a declaration is not executability

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know its runtime condition?
questions.note: live observation with liveness horizon

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know the condition of its knowledge?
questions.note: corpus health, staleness and citation integrity; no knowledge-quality evaluation

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know its decisions and evolution history?
questions.note: Register-derived, append-only

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know its weaknesses and limitations?
questions.note: failures and incompleteness are reported; no evaluation of weakness

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know its self-model has become inaccurate?
questions.note: binding drift is detected; content drift was not (GOAL-V2-005 found 1 of 4 escalations reported)

questions.gloss: Who may declare the self-model valid?
questions.note: validated as part of P12 certification; governance-only

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide what it needs to know?
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: Reasoning concludes which facts an authority-bearing criterion lacks, and which resident verifier produces them (R-OBTAINABLE); NextAction proposes it.

questions.gloss: How does AIOS find a knowledge gap?
questions.note: unresolved citations only; no general gap discovery

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide a knowledge gap matters?
evidence: tools/p13/reasoning.py::An unknown **matters** (Q19, Q89) exactly when an authority-bearing criterion
questions.note: no resident prioritization. P13-018 construction: A knowledge gap matters exactly when an authority-bearing criterion needs it; it escalates as admit.knowledge.

questions.gloss: Where does new knowledge come from?
questions.note: governed admission of promotion candidates

questions.gloss: How does AIOS distinguish information from knowledge?
questions.note: candidate → governed admission; memory CANDIDATE is never eligible

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide a source is trustworthy?
questions.note: human-authorized promotion; no source-trust model

questions.gloss: How does AIOS handle conflicting sources?
questions.note: no resident conflict-resolution mechanism was found; not asserted absent

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know previously true knowledge is stale?
questions.note: governance-corpus staleness; not general knowledge staleness

questions.gloss: How are update, supersession, expiry, invalidation performed?
How does AIOS know what it does not know?
questions.note: scoped to the self-model's own questions; recorded program unknowns are not surfaced

questions.gloss: How does AIOS find a capability gap?
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: R-GAP: an UNKNOWN nothing resident can resolve is a capability gap; Evolution also reads the P13 CORE rows that cite no evidence.

questions.gloss: How does AIOS choose how a gap is resolved?
evidence: tools/p13/evolution.py::a code change is proposed and escalated; P13 never builds itself
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: Resolution is chosen by gap class: verify when evidence is obtainable; otherwise a reserved remedy, which the gate escalates. P13 resolves nothing reserved by itself.

questions.gloss: How does a new capability become official?
questions.note: Department declaration under Founder/governance decision

questions.gloss: How does a capability get a contract?
questions.note: tool contracts, skill declarations

questions.gloss: How is a capability integrated into the runtime?
questions.note: runtime discovery and composition

questions.gloss: How is a capability verified?
questions.note: conformance suites and the P12 verification architecture

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know a new capability improves the system?
questions.note: requires evaluation. P13-018 construction: Every executed action is followed by re-derivation and re-evaluation, and the per-criterion difference is recorded.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: improvement is measured only against the admitted, authority-bearing criteria (before/after re-evaluation). A broader measure of improvement needs its own evaluation contract (FDR-2 D02)

questions.gloss: How is a capability upgraded without breaking others?
questions.note: regression anchors; no capability-level compatibility model

questions.gloss: How is a failed capability suspended, deprecated or retired?
questions.note: tools: DISABLED/RETIRED; no equivalent for capabilities

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know it works well?
questions.note: one bounded health verdict; no system-level evaluation

questions.gloss: What indicates degradation?
questions.note: corpus criteria only

questions.gloss: How are reasoning/knowledge/execution/workflow/decision-support quality measured?
questions.note: 0 Evaluation symbols in native_core. P13-018 construction: reclassified P13 CORE → P13 FRONTIER. P13 measures state against authority-bearing criteria; quality of reasoning, knowledge, execution, workflow and decision-support has no admitted criterion, and FDR-2 D02 requires a measurable intelligence claim to have its own evaluation contract. Residual frontier, classified.

questions.gloss: How does AIOS find previously unknown weaknesses?
questions.note: open research direction

questions.gloss: How does AIOS tell error, limitation, knowledge gap, architecture gap and capability gap apart?
evidence: tools/p13/model.py::# Q40: the kinds of shortfall AIOS tells apart
questions.note: done by humans in governance records; no system mechanism. P13-018 construction: error / limitation / knowledge gap / capability gap / architecture gap, each assigned by rule.

questions.gloss: How does AIOS prioritize repairs?
evidence: tools/p13/next_action.py::**Priority** (Q41, Q63, Q69, Q73) is a fixed rule
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: Fixed rule: defects, then missing evidence, then knowledge gaps, then stale evidence; within a rank, least recently verified per Memory.

questions.gloss: When should AIOS propose change?
questions.note: proposals exist; Optimization → Governance is Architect-reserved (AD-P13-001)

questions.gloss: When must AIOS stop and ask the Founder?
questions.note: out-of-scope work escalates; human authority fails closed

questions.gloss: How does AIOS generate improvement proposals?
questions.note: structure exists; no generation from evaluation

questions.gloss: Where do improvement proposals come from?
questions.note: observations

questions.gloss: How does AIOS prove an improvement is needed?
evidence: tools/p13/evaluation.py::**Missing evidence gives UNKNOWN, never PASS.**
questions.note: requires evaluation. P13-018 construction: An improvement is needed when an authority-bearing criterion FAILs on verified evidence (R-DEFECT); absent evidence proves nothing.

questions.gloss: How are changes to AIOS itself controlled?
questions.note: human authority, certified-evidence barrier, Native Core freeze

questions.gloss: What may AIOS change by itself?
questions.note: resolved by FDR-2 D05 (registered 2026-09-24); was FOUNDER RESERVED. D05: only within an existing valid authority envelope; never self-authorized.

questions.gloss: What may AIOS never change by itself?
questions.note: reserved matters R01–R09 are fixed; the complete P13 list is FDR-2 item 6

questions.gloss: Which changes always need the Founder?
How is a failed improvement rolled back?
questions.note: evidence restoration and versioned history; no runtime rollback model

questions.gloss: How is AIOS's evolution history recorded?
questions.note: append-only Registers, git, supersession ledger

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know a change improves the whole system?
questions.note: system-level evaluation. P13-018 construction: All admitted criteria are re-evaluated after an executed action and the difference is recorded.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: "the whole system" means every admitted criterion, all re-evaluated after an action; nothing wider is claimed (FDR-2 D02)

questions.gloss: How does AIOS connect its domains?
questions.note: 6 of 7 chain relationships bound; Memory ↔ Intelligence not connected

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know component relationships?
questions.note: import graph, integration graph, relationship map

questions.gloss: How does AIOS find side effects of a change?
questions.note: regression anchors and write probe; no general impact analysis

questions.gloss: How does AIOS reason across domains?
questions.note: 0 Reasoning symbols. P13-018 construction: Rules combine facts across domains (governance registers, Knowledge criteria, Memory, certified evidence).
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: deterministic rules over typed facts from governance, knowledge, memory and evidence; no open-ended cross-domain inference (Blueprint §3.4)

questions.gloss: How does AIOS build system-level understanding?
questions.note: a self-model exists; synthesis does not

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know a problem is systemic?
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: Two or more non-PASS results sharing a source are concluded to be one systemic cause.

questions.gloss: How does AIOS manage knowledge to help the Founder?
questions.note: discovery aid, explicitly non-authoritative

questions.gloss: How does AIOS know what context the Founder needs?
evidence: tools/p13/cycle.py::What the Founder needs from this cycle, most pressing first (Q61, Q62)
questions.note: context assembly is a v0.4 candidate surface. P13-018 construction: Each cycle record carries a briefing of escalations and non-PASS criteria.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: the Founder's context is what is escalated to them and what fails their recorded criteria

questions.gloss: How does AIOS compose briefings for the Founder?
evidence: tools/p13/cycle.py::What the Founder needs from this cycle, most pressing first (Q61, Q62)
questions.note: no resident mechanism. P13-018 construction: The cycle composes a briefing (escalations first, then failing criteria, then exhaustion state).

questions.note: no resident prioritization. P13-018 construction: Every criterion cites a Founder-issued instrument; priority follows that.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: answered only as far as the Founder's recorded decisions state it; anything beyond is residual frontier

questions.gloss: How does AIOS find changes the Founder should know?
questions.note: recorded supersession and staleness

questions.gloss: How is Founder decision lineage preserved?
How does AIOS decide what to do next?

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide what to learn first?
evidence: tools/p13/evolution.py::*Learning* here means a proposal into governed admission
questions.note: P13-018 construction: The highest-priority knowledge gap is proposed as admit.knowledge, which escalates.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: learning is a proposal into governed admission, never admission (GAP-0022)

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide which capability to improve first?
questions.note: P13-018 construction: Capability gaps become change.code proposals, escalated in order.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: capability gaps are ordered after defects and missing evidence, and among themselves by identifier only; a value-based ranking is frontier

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide which knowledge to update?
questions.note: P13-018 construction: A missing or unreadable Knowledge input is proposed for governed admission.
questions.p13_status: ANSWERED — BOUNDED: only the admitted corpus-health criteria are Knowledge P13 reads; updating them is a governed revision P13 can only propose

questions.gloss: How does AIOS decide which problem to solve?

questions.note: P13-018 construction: The first proposal by the fixed priority rule; a reserved one escalates instead of executing.
